ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All founding shareholders, directors, UBOs and signatories must be screened, before filing, against (i) Egyptian consolidated sanctions lists and EMLCU directives; (ii) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) OFAC SDN List and OFAC country/entity programs; (iv) EU consolidated financial sanctions list; and (v) local and international PEP databases. Enhanced due diligence applies to any foreign PEP, politically exposed relative or close associate, and to non-resident owners. Screening results and source-of-funds evidence must be documented, kept for at least the period required by Egyptian law, and made available to GAFI/EMLCU on request.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI Investor Service Center (ISC) electronic name reservation system
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official company name must be in Arabic; an English transliteration is registered as a secondary trade name. The Arabic name must not be identical or deceptively similar to a name already reserved in the Commercial Register, must not falsely imply sovereign, banking, insurance, securities or public-corporation objects, and must not include expressions contrary to public order or moral standards.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Religious or sectarian terms (e.g., Islamic, Christian, Mosque, Church)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejected name may be appealed in writing to the GAFI Grievance Committee through the Investor Service Center within 30 days from the rejection notice. The appeal must attach the proposed Arabic name and Latin transliteration, a copy of the rejection, and any prior-authorization letter if a sensitive token is involved. GAFI must issue a reasoned decision within 30 working days. A second rejection may be challenged before the competent administrative judiciary within 60 days from notification. The name reservation may be extended by filing a new application and paying the applicable tariff before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For ISIC 5210/NAICS 493120 cold-chain warehousing, a virtual office is not permissible as the registered address. The registered office must be the actual refrigerated warehouse or an attached administration unit in an approved logistics/industrial property, and must support on-site regulatory inspections by GAFI, the Egyptian Drug Authority and the Ministry of Health.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: HIGH: estimated 75% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months of operation, driven by the cold-chain pharmaceutical license and warehouse safety permit requirements.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 4 of 2023 (Law Promulgating the Companies Law), effective 1 January 2024, Articles 1-4, 57-76 on Limited Liability Companies, read with its Executive Regulations; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations; Commercial Registration Law No. 34 of 1976; Civil Code No. 131 of 1948; and the Egyptians Tax Authority unified tax identification procedures.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Companies Registration Department and Investor One-Stop Shop, Ministry of Investment and Foreign Trade; supporting notarization by the Egyptian Notary Public Authority (Al-Shahr Al-Akari).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Establishment Contract and Memorandum of Articles of Association (Aqd El-Ta'assiss wal-Nizam El-Asasi), executed before the notary public and filed electronically through the GAFI investor portal, culminating in the Certificate of Incorporation and Commercial Registration Certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital applies to LLCs under Law No. 4 of 2023; the founders freely fix the capital in the memorandum. The capital must be fully subscribed, and at least 25% of the cash portion must be paid up before incorporation and deposited into a temporary escrow account ('under-formation account') opened in the company's name at a licensed Egyptian bank. The bank deposit certificate is annexed to the GAFI filing, and the escrow funds are released only upon presentation of the incorporation certificate. In-kind contributions must be fully paid at incorporation and assessed by a licensed expert or the statutory valuation procedure.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY] UNDER FORMATION: RESOLVED: The founding shareholders approve the notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association and ratify the subscription schedule allotting the entire issued share capital to the founders; the paid-up cash quota is lodged in an escrow account opened for the Company at a licensed Egyptian bank and released only against the GAFI incorporation certificate. RESOLVED: The registered office is fixed at the memorandum address, Cairo, Egypt. RESOLVED: The Board of Management is appointed with full powers to complete statutory registrations with GAFI and the Egyptian Tax Authority, to open and manage bank accounts, and to bind the Company in its ordinary business. Adopted unanimously; effective upon incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Company Name and Verify Legal Form Eligibility
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop, Commercial Registry and Investor Services Department, via the Invest in Egypt e-portal (https://www.investinegypt.gov.eg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an electronic name reservation request on the GAFI investor portal, proposing at least three candidate names in Arabic and/or English that identify the activity and the legal form 'LLC'. Verify that the proposed name does not conflict with any existing registered company, trade mark, or reserved name and that the entity structure code for a limited liability company is approved for the ISIC 5210 refrigerated logistics activity. Upon approval, print the name reservation certificate, which remains valid for 90 days, and attach it to the incorporation file.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form signed by each founder or lawful attorney
Copy of valid national IDs of Egyptian founders and passport copies of non-resident founders
Notarized power of attorney with Arabic certified translation if filed by proxy
Declaration of the intended registered office address and contact details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity or conflict, the applicant may submit alternative name candidates within the same reservation window without additional fee, or file a grievance before the GAFI Dispute Settlement Committee within 30 days from notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Authenticate the Memorandum and Articles of Association Before the Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Notary Public Authority (Al-Shahr Al-Akari) or the GAFI One-Stop Shop certified notarial window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After name reservation approval, prepare the Arabic Memorandum and Articles of Association in compliance with Law No. 4 of 2023. Every founder must sign the memorandum before a notary public with proof of identity; remote electronic authentication may be used for local founders on the GAFI notary portal. Non-resident founders must execute a notarized power of attorney, apostilled or legally translated as required. All pages are signed, initialed, and stamped. The notary records the date of authentication, which fixes the formation date of the LLC.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association in Arabic signed by all founders
Original passports or national IDs of all founders for identity verification
Landlord consent or lease contract for the future registered office, or a formal commitment to provide the address within 60 days
Notarized and apostilled power of attorney if signatures are made by proxy
Draft bank escrow mandate if required by the chosen bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary rejects the document for signature defects or missing legalization, the founders must correct the instrument and re-present it; a subsequent notarial appointment within the same week does not attract additional filing fees. Foreign document deficiencies may be cured by obtaining a consular-legalized Arabic certified translation through the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance; official taxpayer portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; e-invoicing, e-receipt, and digital fiscal clearance systems are operated by ETA under the national Tax Digitization Program; physical export clearance is administered by the Egypt Customs Authority (ECA), Ministry of Finance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign-owned Egyptian LLC: (1) obtain commercial registration through the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) and the Egyptian Commercial Register; (2) file a unified tax registration application at the competent ETA tax office using the statutory TIN form, attaching the articles of association, commercial register extract, and executed powers of the local manager(s); (3) receive a single unified Tax Identification Number (TIN) and Tax Card covering Income Tax, VAT, and stamp duties; (4) open a corporate bank account in Egypt and complete e-invoicing/e-receipt enrollment; (5) for export activities, obtain an exporter code at the ECA and reference the ETA TIN in all customs submissions. Non-resident entities without an Egyptian permanent establishment are not issued a local TIN but remain taxable on Egyptian-source income and are subject to VAT at importation through the customs system. Registration by an operating LLC must be completed within 30 days of commencing licensed activity and updated upon any change of address, activity, or management.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch entity classification election exists under Egyptian law; an Egyptian LLC is automatically taxed as a separate resident company under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005. Available limited elections: (i) the simplified/presumptive small and medium enterprise tax regime under Law No. 152 of 2020 for qualifying small and micro projects, subject to ETA eligibility and the revenue ceilings set out in the Executive Regulations; (ii) consolidated tax-group filing under Article 56 of Law No. 91 of 2005 where an Egyptian parent directly holds at least 90 percent of an Egyptian subsidiary's shares and both entities share the same fiscal year, subject to prior ETA approval; and (iii) simplified cash accounting for micro taxpayers where expressly permitted under Law No. 152 of 2020. These elections do not create pass-through or disregarded-entity treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016 (as amended), administered by the Egyptian Tax Authority; supplemented by the Selective or Schedule Tax on tobacco, alcoholic beverages, and hydrocarbon products, and by the e-receipt regime for business-to-consumer retail sales.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 of annual taxable supplies mandates VAT registration; EGP 200,000 of annual turnover permits voluntary registration; registration may also be required for importers and businesses using imported goods/services even where the domestic supply threshold is not exceeded.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All registered taxpayers must issue electronic invoices through ETA-approved channels (webform, REST API, or ERP connector) in the ETA XML-SIG schema; each invoice is transmitted in near-real time to the ETA and passed through centralized validation, with the ETA returning a Unique Invoice Identifier, cryptographic hash, and QR code only after clearance. Only cleared e-invoices are admissible for input-VAT deduction. Business-to-consumer sales are additionally governed by the e-receipt (Iqbal) system requiring per-sale fiscal-code clearance. Cold-storage and logistics operators must integrate warehouse billing systems with ETA APIs, apply sequential fiscal numbering, and retain ETA clearance codes for the statutory five-year record-keeping period.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.vat_grouping_or_fiscal_representative_ru: Foreign entities without an Egyptian establishment may appoint an Egyptian fiscal representative or agent for VAT purposes where required by ETA; Egypt does not generally recognize VAT grouping for separate local LLCs absent consolidation approval under the income tax law.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_place_of_supply_for_cold_st: Cold-storage warehousing services are generally taxable where the warehouseman is established in Egypt; export-linked storage and handling services may be zero-rated when directly connected to physically exported goods and supplied to a non-resident recipient.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.input_vat_recovery_mechanism: Input VAT on rent, electricity, refrigeration equipment, and logistics consumables is creditable against output VAT; excess input VAT arising from zero-rated export activity is refundable through the monthly VAT return and periodic ETA refund procedure, subject to documentary verification.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_filing_frequency: Generally monthly VAT returns with the annual reconciliation; qualifying small taxpayers may be permitted quarterly or simplified returns under ETA administrative practice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The 0% VAT rate is available for: (a) exported goods physically leaving Egypt to a foreign destination without substantial local transformation, evidenced by the customs export declaration; (b) services directly connected with export handling, cold storage, transport, and freight of the same goods where the benefit is received by a non-resident; and (c) other service exports under the place-of-supply rules in the VAT Executive Regulations, where the recipient is established outside Egypt and economic use occurs abroad. Eligibility requires invoicing in foreign currency, actual receipt of the foreign-currency consideration, and cross-matching with the customs declaration, the e-invoice, and the inward remittance record. Cold-storage operators must trace each zero-rated consignment to its export declaration and Cargo Tracking Number; intercompany exports to a foreign affiliate are accepted only at arm's length with full documentation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD) electronically cleared and stamped by the Egypt Customs Authority (ECA)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill or multimodal transport document evidencing removal of goods to a foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or foreign-currency bank receipt issued by a Central Bank of Egypt-licensed bank evidencing receipt and repatriation of export proceeds
ETA-cleared e-invoice bearing the Unique Invoice Identifier and QR code linked to the corresponding export declaration and customs manifest
Certificate of Origin and destination-country health or phytosanitary permits for perishable pharmaceutical, food, and temperature-controlled products, as applicable
Cold-chain temperature log and warehouse storage records demonstrating the goods were held and dispatched in the declared refrigerated condition
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA's Post-Clearance Audit and Automated Risk Model units, together with ECA and the Central Bank of Egypt, cross-match export declarations, cleared e-invoices, freight records, and foreign-exchange receipts. If goods do not physically leave Egypt, or export proceeds are not received and repatriated within the statutory 180-day window, the 0% status is clawed back and VAT at 14% becomes immediately due together with the monthly late-payment charge and administrative fines for non-compliant e-invoicing. Fraudulent export documentation or misdeclaration triggers a punitive addition generally tied to the tax evaded, up to twice the undercharged amount, and criminal liability for responsible officers under Law No. 67 of 2016 and Customs Law No. 207 of 2020, including possible imprisonment, revocation of the exporter code, and joint and several liability of directors and shareholders for duties, taxes, and penalties.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.customs_value_matching_rule: Zero-rated value must reconcile with the customs declared value, the commercial invoice, and the FX receipt; material variances automatically generate ETA audit flags supporting retrospective assessment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), acting in coordination with the Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA), the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), and the Ministry of Finance, pursuant to Law No. 194 of 2020 (Central Bank, Banking and Foreign Exchange Law).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a liberalized, bank-anchored foreign exchange regime in which the Egyptian Pound (EGP) is freely convertible for current account transactions and for approved capital account operations. Capital controls are limited to prior registration of foreign investment through GAFI, strict source-of-funds verification by domestic licensed banks, and documentary embedding of each cross-border flow in the CBE reporting grid. Profit remittances are processed only after distraint of evidenced tax clearance, audited financial statements, and the submitting bank's confirmation of the relevant purpose code; non-resident capital return requires liquidation form submission to the CBE through the customer's Egyptian bank. Since the 2024 unification of the official and market exchange rates, there are no statutory surrender or involuntary conversion ratios, but every hard-currency receipt must flow through the regulated banking channel and be reported on the bank's prudential return.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE directives applicable to the target company, 100% of export proceeds from cold storage services or re-exported pharmaceutical goods must be repatriated into the Egyptian banking system within 6 months from the date of shipment or service performance. The exporter retains full discretion as to whether such proceeds are kept in an Egyptian foreign-currency account or converted into EGP at the prevailing interbank rate; there is no mandatory conversion ratio. The 6-month repatriation obligation is monitored by the collection bank, and failure to repatriate may subject the exporter to CBE penalties and to denial of access to official import-financing facilities. Goods exports additionally require customs-compliant invoice matching under the National Single Window, while service export commissions are admitted on the basis of the underlying service contract and the Ministry of Finance's online services registry.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium. Offshore digital banks and electronic money institutions (EMIs) cannot independently open Egyptian foreign-currency accounts without a CBE license, and Law No. 194 of 2020 restricts the execution of foreign exchange transactions to CBE-licensed banks and authorized payment service providers. Non-bank EMIs domiciled in the EU or MENA hubs may operate only through a local correspondent bank relationship, which largely eliminates their treasury efficiency advantage for this cold-storage project. A CBE-licensed Egyptian fintech such as a digital payment platform may provide collection and disbursement rails, but cross-border clearing and FX conversion must still be settled through a tier-1 banking counterparty.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory. Under CBE Know-Your-Customer rules and Egypt's AML/CFT Law No. 80 of 2002, the LLC's authorized signatories and ultimate beneficial owners must appear in person at the mandated bank branch for an interview and original-document verification. Remote account opening is not generally available for corporate vehicles; at minimum, the general manager or a director holding a duly notarized and apostilled board resolution must physically attend the onboarding session. Egyptian commercial banks may additionally require a site visit to the registered address and to the temperature-controlled facility to validate operational substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholders and opaque chain of ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate extract from the home registry showing the full shareholding chain, apostilled and legalized board resolution authorizing account opening, original director passport copies, specimen signatures certified before a notary, and a completed CBE beneficial-ownership declaration identifying every individual above the 25% threshold.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cold-storage business perceived as a high-volume cash-heavy logistics operation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid refrigeration/warehousing licenses issued by the Ministry of Health and Population or the General Authority for Food Safety, ISIC 5210 certificate, GAFI establishment number, leased or owned storage capacity proof, utility bills, and a signed compliance statement confirming that no cash settlement shall be made above the statutory threshold.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of inward capital or shareholder loans
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank confirmation letters covering the last 12 months, audited financial statements of the source entity, notarized shareholder loan agreements, and a CBE source-of-funds statement supported by underlying invoices or dividend approval documents; the entire bundle must be apostilled and professionally translated for submission.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Regulated pharmaceutical goods triggering trade-based money-laundering review
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Licensed drug storage permits, product/identity files, temperature-logging maintenance records, end-client warehousing agreements, customs declarations, and the GCC/Pharmaceutical Exchange membership certificate where applicable.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital, shareholder advances, and long-term project funding must be wired exclusively through SWIFT MT103 or MT202 messages into the LLC's EGP-designated or foreign-currency account at a licensed Egyptian bank. Each transfer requires a precise CBE purpose code (asset subscription or FDI capital contribution code), and the receiving bank must file the CBE FDI declaration with the repo of the transaction; the wire is credited only after the bank verifies the underlying GAFI certificate and the match between the remitter's name, the share ledger, and the board resolution. For the target cold-storage facility, capital injections should be structured as registered equity rather than loans to avoid circularity penalties under the CBE's external debt reporting regime. Each receivable is routed through the interbank EGP counterparty to be cleared at the official exchange rate, and the resulting EGP balances are fungible across the operational working capital account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements utilize SWIFT MT103 for direct service fees, MT700 documentary letters of credit for imports of refrigeration equipment or pharmaceutical inventory, and the Egyptian Central Securitization and Settlement Co. (EGCS) clearing for EGP-denominated payments. Local payments are settled via the Egyptian Payment Network (EGN) and the CBE Real-Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) system, while cross-border supplier payments require invoice matching, customs declarations, and the submitting bank's percentage check against the LLC's approved export generation. USD-denominated outflows may be constrained by the CBE's prudential limits on banks' net open foreign-currency positions, and the treasury should prioritize matching inbound EGP purchase flows with scheduled outbound trade dues.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore EGP/USD deliverable forwards concluded with a licensed Egyptian commercial bank, backed by a genuine current-account or investment-account exposure
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) traded with international banks through the non-resident overlay, subject to CBE mark-to-market documentation
Cross-currency swap agreements executed exclusively with CBE-authorized bank counterparties for long-term refrigeration equipment procurement
FX forward with a correlation in the global commodity cold-chain treasury to collar a portion of the EGP/USD closing price exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the close of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late-payment penalty on outstanding tax plus late-filing penalty of EGP 2,000 to EGP 20,000; continued failure may trigger license block and administrative strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Annual Financial Statements and Directors' Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the close of the financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines per Companies Law up to EGP 50,000 and possible delisting from commercial register for repeated default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Commercial Registry (Ministry of Trade and Industry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: During January and February of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal fee equal to 50% of the annual registration fee; continuation after 30 days can lead to administrative strike-off and de-registration of the entity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Warning followed by administrative fines up to EGP 50,000 and suspension of the company's commercial registration rights.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit for all LLCs whose capital exceeds EGP 1 million, whose annual turnover exceeds EGP 10 million, or whose shareholders so request under the Egyptian Companies Law; otherwise audit is required for tax purposes if accounting records fail to meet statutory standards.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), which are converged with IFRS for statutory reporting; IFRS itself accepted for certain multinational groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each LLC must maintain a beneficial ownership register and file an annual confirmation with GAFI, disclosing any transfers of shares or ultimate beneficial ownership changes within 30 days; the annual confirmation must re-affirm the identity and nationality of each UBO and any direct ownership percentages.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 - USD 400 per annum for a registered office address; USD 500 - USD 1,200 per annum for a professional corporate service provider in Cairo
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 800 - USD 2,500 per annum for a small LLC cold chain logistics company under Egyptian Accounting Standards

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Egyptian LLCs pay corporate income tax at 22.5% under Law 91/2005 Article 8. Qualifying refrigerated-logistics projects may reduce the effective rate through: (1) Investment Law No. 72/2017 as amended by Law 173/2023 tax incentives, providing a 30-50% reduction of the annual CIT liability computed on the project paid-in capital or investment cost, applied for up to 7 years for strategic cold-chain and logistics projects; (2) prior-regime projects obtaining a 50% deduction of investment costs from taxable profits where registration predates the 2023 amendment; (3) General Free Zone and Suez Canal Economic Zone licensed LLCs engaged in export-oriented warehousing enjoying a full CIT exemption on qualifying profits; (4) ordinary deductions for cost of goods sold, depreciation of refrigerated equipment at 25% straight-line, warehouse buildings, and arm's-length financing costs.
